title: 对称 Y–Y 三相四线制电路
statement: 对称三相电源（正序，相电压 U̇_A = 220∠0° V）通过三根端线和一根中线向对称星形负载供电，每相负载 Z = 40 + j30 Ω。电流表 A_N 串在中线上，测量从 N' 流向 N 的中线电流 İ_N。
求 A 相电流的有效值、B 相电流 İ_B 的初相（参考方向见图）和中线电流表的读数。

questions.ask: A 相电流有效值 I_A = ?
questions.explain: 有中线且中线阻抗为零，U̇_N'N = 0，每相负载直接承受相电压：I_A = 220/|40 + j30| = 220/50 = 4.4 A。

questions.ask: 中线电流表 A_N 的读数 = ?
questions.explain: İ_N = İ_A + İ_B + İ_C，三个电流大小相等、互差 120°，相量和为零。

questions.ask: 如果把这条中线断开，各相电流会怎样？
choices: 不变——对称负载时中性点 N' 与 N 本来就等电位，中线中没有电流
都变为零，因为没有了回路
A 相电流增大，B、C 相电流减小
choiceExplain: 电流可以经另外两根端线返回电源（三相三线制）；中线只承担三相电流之和，而对称时这个和为零。
各相电流只会随中性点位移 U̇_N'N 而变化，而中性点位移只在负载不对称时出现；本题三相负载相同，A 相并没有特殊之处。
1/√3 是把相电压和线电压混淆了；断开中线后每相负载仍然承受相电压 220 V。
questions.explain: 对称 Y–Y 电路中 U̇_N'N = 0、İ_N = 0，中线有无对电路没有影响（三相三线制也能正常工作）。电流仍可经另外两根端线返回电源，并不需要中线。

hints: 对称 Y–Y 电路可以“归结为一相”计算：只画 A 相（U̇_A 与 Z 串联，N' 与 N 用短路线相连）。
求出 İ_A 后，İ_B、İ_C 按对称关系依次滞后 120°。
中线电流 İ_N = İ_A + İ_B + İ_C。
solution: **4. 结论。** 对称三相电路中线电流为零，中线可以省去；负载的功率因数 cos36.87° = 0.8（感性）。

en.title: Balanced Y–Y four-wire circuit
statement: A balanced three-phase source (positive sequence, phase voltage U̇_A = 220∠0° V) feeds a balanced wye load through three lines and a neutral wire; each phase of the load is Z = 40 + j30 Ω. Ammeter A_N in the neutral wire measures the neutral current İ_N flowing from N' to N.
Find the rms value of the phase-A current, the phase of İ_B (reference directions as drawn) and the reading of the neutral ammeter.

questions.ask: rms current of phase A, I_A = ?
questions.explain: With a zero-impedance neutral, U̇_N'N = 0 and each load phase sees its phase voltage: I_A = 220/|40 + j30| = 220/50 = 4.4 A.

questions.ask: Reading of the neutral ammeter A_N = ?
questions.explain: İ_N = İ_A + İ_B + İ_C: three equal currents 120° apart add up to zero.

questions.ask: If the neutral wire is cut, what happens to the phase currents?
choices: Nothing changes — with a balanced load N' and N are already at the same potential and the neutral carries no current
They all become zero, because the return path is gone
The phase-A current increases and the B and C currents decrease
Each phase current becomes 1/√3 of its old value
choiceExplain: The currents return through the other two line conductors (a three-wire system); the neutral only carries the sum of the three currents, which is zero here.
The phase currents can change only through a neutral-point displacement U̇_N'N, which arises only with an unbalanced load; here the three phases are identical, so nothing singles out phase A.
The factor 1/√3 confuses phase and line voltage; with the neutral open each load phase still sees the 220 V phase voltage.
questions.explain: In a balanced Y–Y circuit U̇_N'N = 0 and İ_N = 0, so the neutral makes no difference (a three-wire system works just as well). The currents return to the source through the other lines; no neutral is needed.

hints: A balanced Y–Y circuit reduces to a single-phase calculation: draw only phase A (U̇_A in series with Z, with N' and N joined by a short).
Once you have İ_A, İ_B and İ_C follow by symmetry, each lagging by another 120°.
The neutral current is İ_N = İ_A + İ_B + İ_C.
solution: **1. Per-phase equivalent.** In a balanced circuit U̇_N'N = 0, so phase A can be solved alone: Z = 40 + j30 = 50∠36.87° Ω, İ_A = U̇_A/Z = 220∠0°/50∠36.87° = **4.4∠−36.87° A**, rms value **4.4 A**.
**3. Neutral current.** İ_N = İ_A + İ_B + İ_C = 4.4∠−36.87° × (1 + 1∠−120° + 1∠120°) = **0**, so the ammeter reads 0 A.
**4. Conclusion.** In a balanced three-phase circuit the neutral current is zero and the neutral wire can be omitted; the load power factor is cos36.87° = 0.8 (inductive).
